chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
A man from the people of Sijistān came to him and said: “We have dirhams called al-Shāmiyyah that carry two dāniqs more than the dirhams.”
So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it; that is permissible.”

key_terms.الشَّامِيَّةُ: a type of dirham known by this regional designation
key_terms.دَانِقَيْنِ: two dāniqs, a small unit of monetary value
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection in it
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: it is permissible or valid in law

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange dirhams that have a higher recognized value than other dirhams?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning currency exchange involving a type of dirham that had an added value over standard dirhams. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that such a difference in value is permissible, indicating allowance for recognized monetary variation in commercial dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4040 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that

a man from Sijistan came to him and said:
"We have dirhams called al-Shamiyyah that are valued two daniqs more than regular dirhams."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it; it is permissible."
